why_it_moved.text: Queries per User fell 1.9% while Clicks per User (+0.1%) and Sessions per User (-0.1%) stayed flat, so per-query rates like CTR (+2.1%) can rise with no better results.
why_it_moved.label: inferred

why_it_moved.text: Successful Search Rate rose 0.81%, but Long Click Rate, Abandonment Rate and Reformulation Rate did not move, and no query class or device shows a clear gain.
why_it_moved.label: measured

why_it_moved.text: Ranker v7 may have cut repeat or accidental queries, which would be a real gain, but nothing on the scorecard shows it yet.
why_it_moved.label: guess

would_change: Success per user (not per query) flat while queries fall: the lift is the denominator, so the bar is not met.
Success on queries where ranking changed up clearly, with untriggered queries flat: a real relevance gain.
A pre-exposure comparison showing the arms already differed before the test started.

analyst_view.reason: The primary is a per-query rate and queries per user fell while clicks stayed flat; this may be the denominator, not better ranking.
